title: GEMQ: Global Expert-Level Mixed-Precision Quantization for MoE LLMs
claim: Component importance varies heterogeneously across and within layers, and compression substantially distorts routing decisions, motivating global allocation and router adaptation.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right; heatmap with bar chart beneath, line plot right
description: Two-panel empirical figure. Panel (a), left, shows a heatmap titled 'Expert-wise Squared Gradient Distribution (Sum over Parameters)'. Layer index (0–31) runs along the x-axis and expert index (0–7) along the y-axis. Cells are shaded in blues, with a colorbar from about 100 to 700+. Most cells are pale, and a few are dark. The darkest is at layer 30, expert 2. Under the heatmap, a blue bar chart labeled 'Layer Sum' gives per-layer totals, with a large spike at layer 30 and a smaller one near layer 18. Panel (b), right, is a green line plot with circular markers titled 'Expert Selection Change Ratio'. It plots the percentage of tokens routed to different experts against layer index. The curve rises from about 8% at layer 0 to a peak above 50% near layer 24, then dips slightly. The eye goes first to the dark heatmap cell, then to the green curve.
caption: Motivations. (a) The sensitivity of expert weights, measured by squared gradients (\ie, the trace of the empirical Fisher Information Matrix), varies not only within a layer but also across layers, indicating heterogeneous layer importance; and (b) over 40% of tokens are routed to different experts after 1.5-bit quantization, revealing substantial distortion in router distributions. Statistics are computed from the Mixtral-8$\times$7B model on WikiText2.
abstract: Mixture-of-Experts Large Language Models (MoE-LLMs) achieve strong performance but incur substantial memory overhead due to massive expert parameters. Mixed-precision quantization mitigates this cost by allocating expert-wise bit-widths based on their importance, approaching the accuracy-memory Pareto frontier and enabling extreme low-bit quantization. However, existing methods rely on layer-wise importance estimation and overlook router shifts induced by quantization, resulting in suboptimal allocation and routing. In this work, we propose Global Expert-level Mixed-precision Quantization (GEMQ) to overcome these limitations via (1) a global linear-programming formulation that captures model-wide expert importance based on quantization error analysis, and (2) efficient router fine-tuning to adapt routing to quantized experts. These components are integrated into a progressive quantization framework that iteratively refines importance estimation and allocation. Experiments demonstrate that GEMQ significantly reduces memory and accelerates inference with minimal accuracy degradation. Source code is available at https://github.com/jndeng/GEMQ .
